current_objectives: Determine whether the two paper-reported material-specific constant surface anchors reduce joint supported-row log-profile error by at least 50% relative to the better common-anchor control while the material-specific constant-D anchor, thermal history, equation, initial condition, and reduction are frozen.

Determine whether the resolved low-concentration support length and the boundary decision change materially when shared-occlusion rows and rows at or below 3 x 10^15 cm^-3 are admitted by exact preregistered masks.
frozen_invariants: Use only the two supplied legend-bound CSV series. Preserve panel_key, series_key, point_index, x_value, y_value, x_uncertainty, y_uncertainty, observed, quantitative_measurement_claim_eligible, below_sims_detection_limit, support_kind, pixel coordinates, coordinate_ownership, shared_group, and support_source_series exactly; never fill a missing point index or treat a shared-occlusion row as independent.

The pre-execution audit must reproduce the exact headers and categorical values. The supplied tables contain 501 In0.83Al0.17As rows and 765 In0.83Ga0.17As rows; support_kind is direct_pixel or shared_occlusion; all observed and eligibility values are 1; all supplied below_sims_detection_limit flags are 0 despite 104 and 10 respective central y_value values at or below 3 x 10^15 cm^-3.

Freeze three decision-bearing masks from actual fields and require y_value>y_uncertainty so the declared two-sided log perturbation is finite. M0 selects observed=1, quantitative_measurement_claim_eligible=1, support_kind=direct_pixel, y_value>3 x 10^15 cm^-3, and y_value>y_uncertainty, yielding exactly 359 InAlAs and 702 InGaAs rows. M1 uses the same predicates except support_kind may be direct_pixel or shared_occlusion, yielding exactly 383 and 753 rows. M2 selects observed eligible rows of either support_kind with y_value>y_uncertainty, yielding exactly 439 and 757 rows; it is sensitivity evidence only because numeric central values conflict with the all-zero limit flags. These aggregate counts are supplied by the bound review; the exact row identities and adjacency ledgers are a required pre-implementation reproduction, not claimed as already verified.

Also freeze central-value-only sensitivity masks S0-S2 using the prior M0-M2 predicates without y_value>y_uncertainty: S0 contains 373 InAlAs and 702 InGaAs rows, S1 contains 397 and 755, and S2 contains 501 and 765. Thus S0 adds 14 affected InAlAs rows; S1 adds those 14 plus 2 affected InGaAs shared rows; S2 adds 62 affected InAlAs and 8 affected InGaAs rows relative to the corresponding finite masks. Compute central WRMSE, G, T, and category on S0-S2 without uncertainty envelopes. These checks may force an otherwise supported or rejected disposition to inconclusive if the category changes, but cannot create support or rejection. Reproduce exact excluded-row identities and adjacency effects from the supplied tables before implementation; do not infer them from aggregate counts.

For M0 and S0 every selected row has unit weight. For M1, M2, S1, and S2 define dependence_group as nonblank shared_group; otherwise use the exact tuple panel_key, pixel_x_raw, pixel_y_raw. Give every row in group g weight 1/n_g across both series so a shared source pixel contributes total weight one. No missing or blank provenance field may be guessed.

Temperature is exactly 480 degrees C and elapsed time is exactly 480 s. For material m solve partial C_m/partial t = D_m partial squared C_m/partial x squared on 0<x<L with C_m(x,0)=0, C_m(0,t)=Cs, and C_m(L,t)=0. Use D_Al=1.59 x 10^-12 cm^2/s and D_Ga=1.05 x 10^-12 cm^2/s only as paper-reported anchors.

Set L=x_max+6 sqrt(D_max t), with x_max the deepest existing target x_value, D_max=1.59 x 10^-12 cm^2/s, and t=480 s. The only physical intervention is Cs at 6.85 x 10^19 or 8.35 x 10^19 cm^-3. Do not fit D or Cs, add a source history, add a transport channel, or identify a defect species.

Sample predicted C only at each existing x_value. For a decision-mask row i, y_i=log10(y_value_i/(cm^-3)); define the two exact log perturbations d_y,i^- = y_i-log10((y_value_i-y_uncertainty_i)/(cm^-3)) and d_y,i^+ = log10((y_value_i+y_uncertainty_i)/(cm^-3))-y_i. The finite-mask predicate guarantees both are finite. Use x_i^- = max(0,x_value_i-x_uncertainty_i) and x_i^+ = min(L,x_value_i+x_uncertainty_i). Preserve the asymmetric y perturbations and exact clipped x endpoints in the deterministic envelope; do not collapse them into a standard uncertainty or assign a distribution. Record the absolute primary-versus-tightened log-prediction difference u_num,i at the same x_value. Rows with y_value<=y_uncertainty enter only S0-S2 central-value sensitivity and have no claimed uncertainty interval.

For material m, boundary anchor a, and mask k compute WRMSE_m,a,k=sqrt(sum(w_i*(log10(Cpred_m,a(x_i))-y_i)^2)/sum(w_i)) using only finite positive predictions and selected rows. Define J_own,k=sqrt((WRMSE_Al,low,k squared+WRMSE_Ga,high,k squared)/2), J_low,k from both low-anchor cells, J_high,k from both high-anchor cells, and G_k=1-J_own,k/min(J_low,k,J_high,k). G is unavailable if any component is unavailable or the common-anchor denominator is nonpositive.

Define resolved low-concentration support length T_m,k without a threshold crossing: sort selected rows by point_index and sum x_value_i-x_value_previous only when the indices differ by exactly one and both central concentrations are below 5.4 x 10^16 cm^-3; for M0 and M1 both must also exceed 3 x 10^15 cm^-3, while M2 has no lower concentration cutoff. Never add length across a missing index. Report T separately by material and mask.

Construct a deterministic sensitivity envelope with no probability or coverage interpretation. For each reported scalar Q (each WRMSE, J, G, T, and relative T change), compute nominal Q0 on a frozen finite mask. For each dependence_group g in turn, coherently recompute Q at the four joint corners formed by every row in g taking its lower or upper y perturbation and its clipped lower or upper x endpoint, while all other groups remain nominal; define b_g(Q) as the largest absolute corner departure from Q0. Preserve a shared group jointly across materials. Define b_num(Q) as the largest absolute departure obtained by coherently replacing all predictions contributing to Q with their paired tightened predictions. Set B_Q=sum_g b_g(Q)+b_num(Q) and report E_Q=[Q0-B_Q,Q0+B_Q] without truncation. This additive one-group-at-a-time envelope is a preregistered deterministic sensitivity bound, not a confidence interval; it neither assumes independence nor multiplies by 1.96. If any required corner, bound, denominator, or endpoint is unavailable or nonfinite, E_Q is unavailable and the associated disposition is inconclusive.

The supplied rows at the 5.4 x 10^16 cm^-3 crossing remain structurally discontinuous between point_index 447 and 466 for InAlAs and 363 and 382 for InGaAs. No current quantity depends on interpolating those crossings. The old F, E, qualified-dose, Delta, and R definitions are explicitly deferred and are not execution prerequisites.

No disposition from this study establishes kick-out, VCD, a continuous microscopic response, or any other defect mechanism. Claims are restricted to adequacy and relative performance of the frozen constant-D, constant-boundary family and to robustness of the pixel-derived low-concentration support.

value_assessment.rationale: The current-objective selection is unchanged because this round still covers both original mandatory observables: finite M0 whole-profile errors use the two material-resolved profiles, while T and its finite-mask plus excluded-row sensitivity quantify the observed low-concentration front/tail contrast only over contiguous existing rows. This revision removes the two reviewed blockers by requiring y_value>y_uncertainty in decision masks and replacing unsupported probabilistic intervals with additive deterministic sensitivity envelopes. The bound review supplies aggregate revised counts but not exact revised row identities or adjacency ledgers, so the formal pre-implementation audit must reproduce those items and execution cannot claim they were already checked. The unavailable threshold-crossing F, tail extent from F, qualified dose, Delta, and R remain deferred because both crossings lie across missing point indices. Microscopic continuous-versus-two-regime discrimination also remains deferred until the constant-boundary family is rejected or ambiguous, passes adequacy, and the direct-pixel above-limit low-concentration contrast is stable. These omissions do not invalidate the current supported-row loss or no-gap mask-sensitivity calculations, but they restrict claims to the frozen constant-D boundary counterfactual and pixel-derived evidence robustness. The design remains minimal: four physical cells and four paired convergence controls, three finite masks plus deterministic postprocessing of their broader central-value counterparts, no fitted parameter, no stochastic model, and no extra solve. Information gain remains medium because model inadequacy, unavailable ledgers, wide envelopes, or excluded-row sensitivity can still force inconclusive. Later microscopic work requires a separately reviewed finite model family; stronger empirical claims require qualified raw SIMS data.
